audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[0].text, spikes[1].text, early and whys[0] all say Karma does not have Mantra before level 6 ("before she has Mantra", "Karma's real spike is 6").
audit.why: Riot's own text on Mantra: "Mantra is available at level 1 and does not require a skill point." It is live from the first second of the game — level 6 only ranks it up. A Jayce told he has a Mantra-free window will walk into an empowered Inner Flame or a Mantra-Focused Resolve root at level 3 and not understand what happened. Gathering Fire (P) compounds it: every damaging ability she lands cuts Mantra's 40s cooldown, so trading chip into her actively speeds up the tool the page says she does not have yet.
audit.corrected: Mantra is live from level 1 without a skill point; level 6 ranks it up. Gathering Fire shortens its 40s cooldown every time she lands damage.

audit.whatIsWrong: Focused Resolve is named eleven times across both layers but its cooldown, its range and the condition that breaks it are never given.
audit.why: Focused Resolve is a flat 12s at every rank, 675 range, and the root only lands if the tether survives — Riot: "If the tether is not broken, the enemy will be rooted." Thundering Blow's 600-unit knockback from 240 range puts you outside 675, which is exactly why the existing advice to knock her out of it works. Stating the number turns a vague instruction into a check the player can actually run, and 12s flat means it never gets safer to bait.
audit.corrected: 12s flat, 675-range tether, breaks on distance or LoS — knocked past it, the root never completes.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing in either layer mentions Grievous Wounds, despite the matchup being decided by extended trades.
audit.why: _missing-interactions.json flags this matchup for anti-heal, and the kit backs it: Mantra-empowered Focused Resolve heals Karma while it roots. In a lane the page tells you to win by chip and repeat poke, a heal attached to her main CC is the thing that undoes the whole plan, and the timing of the anti-heal purchase is what decides whether the poke lead survives past first item.
audit.corrected: Buy Grievous Wounds before committing to extended trades — Mantra-Focused Resolve heals her through the chip.

audit.why: The spike set is right in shape: Jayce spikes at 2-3 when Acceleration Gate unlocks the accelerated Shock Blast, Karma at 6 and on item. The only factual repair needed was what level 6 does for her (rank-up, not arrival), which does not move the spike itself. Jayce's own spikes are correctly placed — E at 2, first item, two items — and the levelChart's Jayce-favoured 2/3 matches the gate coming online.

50.73% over 2657 games and a chart with no permanent owner is internally consistent, and the prose reads it correctly: Jayce owns levels 2-3 and the first-item window, Karma owns scaling and teamfights. Difficulty 6/10 with an EVEN label matches the number.

edits.before: Karma's Inner Flame (Q) is a long poke missile, but pre-6 it does not out-range your accelerated gate-Q, so fire Shock Blast through the Acceleration Gate at her step-ups and win the range war before she has Mantra. The thing that flattens your chip is her Inspire (E) -- it shields the orb damage and gives her move speed to walk out, so do not throw a gate-Q into a fresh shield. Bait the E, then commit the Cannon-Q and follow with the R swap-shred when she has no shield up.
edits.after: Karma's Inner Flame (Q) is a 950-range poke missile on 9s at rank 1, so fire Shock Blast through the Acceleration Gate at her step-ups and trade on that gap. Mantra is available from level 1 without a skill point, and Gathering Fire (P) shaves its 40s cooldown every time she lands damage -- so eating chip is what arms her. Her Inspire (E) shield, 10s at rank 1, absorbs the orb and speeds her out; bait it, then commit Cannon-Q into the R swap-shred.

edits.before: At 6 the math tilts to her: Mantra empowers Inner Flame into a wider double-poke and turns Focused Resolve (W) into a long-leash root that locks you for a gank, so respect the tether range and hug your wave. Your level 6 adds nothing -- the R stance-swap is the same tool you had at level 1 -- so this is her window, not yours. Your out is Thundering Blow (Hammer E): knock her out of the Focused Resolve channel before the root snaps on, and keep the wave on your side so she has to walk into accelerated-Q range to do anything.
edits.after: At 6 Mantra ranks up rather than arrives: the empowered Inner Flame widens and Mantra-Focused Resolve becomes a longer root that heals her, so buy Grievous Wounds before you commit to any extended trade or the chip you spent the early game banking gets healed back. Your level 6 adds nothing -- the R stance-swap is the same tool you had at level 1. Your out is Thundering Blow (Hammer E), 20s at rank 1: the knockback drags you past the 675-range tether, and Focused Resolve breaks on distance, so the root never completes. Keep the wave on your side.
